name: Halversen Ironweave Coverall — Standard Cut
description: One-piece charcoal coverall in heavy ironweave canvas, double-stitched at every stress point and pre-worn to a soft matte finish. Chest pocket with a name-badge slot and a faded union patch on the left sleeve. Cut straight through the hips with no taper — functional, not flattering.
functionality: Oil-resistant finish, knee padding inserts, and full-length front zip with snap storm placket for cold-weather sealing.
what_it_says: You work with your body, you've worn this a hundred times, and you'll wear it a hundred more.
story_hooks: The union patch on the sleeve belongs to a local that was officially dissolved two years ago — some workers still wear them as quiet defiance.
A technician finds a folded note tucked inside the chest pocket lining of a secondhand coverall — coordinates and a time, nothing else.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian one-piece silhouette that hangs straight from shoulders to ankles, projecting no-nonsense durability. The coverall reads as work-worn authenticity—neither tailored nor baggy, but deliberately proportioned for function over form. On-body presence suggests someone who builds, repairs, or maintains infrastructure.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed straight-cut through the torso and hips with no taper; generous in the thigh and calf. Cut to accommodate movement and layering underneath. Sleeves sit at mid-forearm with a slight taper. Collar sits flat and wide.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy ironweave canvas—a ballistic-grade synth-natural blend (60% treated hemp composite, 40% synthetic reinforcement fibers). Matte finish from industrial pre-washing.
physical_description.texture: Soft but rigid canvas with a visible weave pattern. Surface is slightly pilled from wear. Double-stitched seams create subtle ridge texture along stress points (shoulders, crotch, sleeve hems). Faded to a uniform charcoal-gray with no sheen.
physical_description.color_scheme: Muted charcoal gray with darker charcoal topstitching. Faded union patch on left sleeve in faded red and white. Name-badge slot appears as a slightly lighter rectangular ghost from repeated use.
physical_description.closures: Full-length heavy-duty brass YKK slider zipper down center front from neck to groin. Concealed snap buttons at collar. Reinforced belt loops (no belt included).
distinctive_features: Chest pocket with embroidered name-badge slot and faded union seal patch
Double-stitching at all stress points (shoulders, underarms, crotch seam, hem)
Pre-worn matte finish—intentionally broken-in by manufacturer
Halversen Workwear Co. woven label at neck (faded)
Subtle wear creases at elbows and knees from factory treatment
Tool loops on thighs (left and right)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional working-class. Affordable durability, not luxury.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by infrastructure workers, maintenance crews, factory floor personnel, and ungoverned-sector salvagers. Signals honest labor and union affiliation (historical). Common in GLMZ dockside, industrial sectors, and remote station repair crews. Occasionally worn ironically by Tier 2 youth.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and weathered on arrival. Creases at joints, faded color gradients from sun and sweat, small stains or scuffs normalized as part of the aesthetic. Designed to look lived-in immediately.
